answer: Each identity monthly launches one instrumented weather balloon from the harbor, its payload carrying an opal reflector and a transmitter that answers live nonces while rising to the vertex of its logged ascent. Independent receivers verify the track matches wind records within 10% and that the nonce replies could not be replayed. A balloon, helium and tracker cost about $210 and are lost on burst, so 1,000 Sybils cost $210,000 monthly with no reuse. Trade-off: launches need airspace permits, create waste, and cap admission at about 20 per day.
